# Git workflow

This condenses S §7 for agents. The project's own policy is `docs/git-workflow.md`. Where the two differ,
the project's policy wins.

## Hard limits

- **Never** add or change a remote, push, push tags, open pull requests, or request branch protection.
  People do those things. Prepare the exact command instead.
- **Never** rewrite published history, force-push, or delete someone else's branch.
- **Never** run destructive commands without the user's explicit instruction in this session. That covers
  `git reset --hard`, `git clean -fd`, `git checkout -- <path>`, `git stash drop`, `git branch -D`, and
  `git push --force`. Prefer recoverable alternatives (S §7.26).
- **Never** commit secrets, `.env` files, `target/`, local databases, editor state, or personal Git
  configuration (S §7.14, §7.20). If a secret was committed, stop and report it. Removing it from the tree
  does not revoke it.
- **Never** commit on the default branch directly. Integration into it follows the release decision.

## Branches (S §7.5)

- Name the branch `<prefix>/<card-id>-<short-slug>`. The prefix is one of `feature/`, `fix/`, `security/`,
  `refactor/`, `docs/`, or `chore/`.
- Keep lowercase and hyphens. Keep vulnerability details and customer data out of the name.
- Branch from the up-to-date default branch. Keep one card per branch, with a life of hours or days.
- Update the branch from the default branch using the policy in `docs/git-workflow.md`, rebase or merge
  (brief §18). Only rebase commits that are not yet published.

```bash
git switch <default-branch>
git switch -c feature/<card-id>-<slug>
```

## Staging and commits (S §7.7 to §7.9)

1. Inspect the tree with `git status --short` and `git diff`.
2. Stage explicit paths that belong to the card: `git add <path>…`. Avoid `git add .` and `git add -A`
   as a habit. Look hard at lockfiles, fixtures, and generated files.
3. Check what is staged with `git diff --staged`.
4. Commit with a message in this shape:

```text
<Imperative subject saying what the commit does, 72 characters or fewer>

<Why the change is needed, and any non-obvious tradeoff. Call out breaking
behavior, migrations, and operational effects.>

Kanban: <card-id>
```

Each commit is one coherent change, buildable where practical, and safe to revert (S §7.8). Record the full
ID with `git rev-parse HEAD`. That ID is the candidate that later stages judge.

## Candidate and evidence commits

A candidate is the immutable commit whose product content later stages judge. After it exists, the
orchestrator may create local evidence commits that only append under `work-items/<card-id>.md`'s
`## Log`. Before each evidence commit, inspect both the staged path and diff; any other change means the
new product-changing commit must become a new candidate.

Therefore the candidate need not remain branch head. It must remain an ancestor of the head, and every
intervening commit must be evidence-only for the same card. Never amend a candidate merely to insert its own
ID into the log: a commit cannot contain its own final ID.

## Parallel work (S §7.23)

Two cards in progress at once need separate worktrees, never two stashes or one mixed tree:

```bash
git worktree add ../<project>-<card-id> -b feature/<card-id>-<slug> <default-branch>
```

Remove the worktree with `git worktree remove` once the card is integrated.

## Conflicts and recovery (S §7.25, §7.26)

- Resolve a conflict by understanding both sides. Rerun the tests after resolving, and record the
  resolution in the commit body.
- Recover first with non-destructive tools: `git reflog`, `git revert`, and new branches from known
  commits.

## Integration and tags

- Merge into the default branch only after the release decider's go (see `rust-release-readiness`). Use
  the brief §18 strategy: squash, rebase-and-merge, or a merge commit.
- A release tag follows the project's scheme, is created locally, and is pushed by a person.

## Traceability (S §7.30)

The chain is card → branch → candidate commit → integration commit → tag → released artifact. Record each
link in the work-item log as it happens. Merging records a commit. It does not close the card, unless
brief §10 makes merge the delivery point.
